simple.meaning: מַעֲנָה (maʻănâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a furrow.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across 1 Samuel, Psalms, beginning at 1 Samuel 14:14. Its contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲנָה (H4618).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַעֲנָה (maʻănâh) / H4618 is traced through 1 Samuel 14:14, Psalms 129:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H4618. maanah מַעֲנָה noun feminine place for task (?), specifically field for ploughing : — plural suffix לְמַעֲנוֺתָם Psa 129:3 Kt they have extended their ploughing-grounds (Qr מַעֲנִיתָם ); singular מַעֲנָה only 1Sam 14:14 , where text corrupt and meaning dubious see Commentaries מַעֲנִית Psa 129:3 Qr see foregoing.
definitions.rootNote: from 6031 , in the sense of depression or tilling;

occurrences.englishText: That first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armor bearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were half a furrow’s length in an acre of land.
The plowers plowed on my back.
